firms.name: Alpine Investors
firms.notes: Founder and lead sponsor of Apex Service Partners (est. 2019), the largest US residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform.

tags.description: Oct 2023 ~$3.4B single-asset continuation-fund transaction for Apex — among the largest in PE history — let Alpine return capital to investors while retaining the asset; in May 2026 Apollo Funds took a ~$2B minority stake at a $10B valuation, capitalizing the rollup further.

firms.name: Ares Management
firms.notes: Co-majority owner of Aspen Dental Management (with Leonard Green & Partners; American Securities holds a minority stake).

firms.name: Blackstone
firms.notes: Took TeamHealth private in 2017 (its second time owning the firm). Co-investors include CDPQ, PSP Investments and Korea's National Pension Service.

firms.name: Formation Capital
firms.notes: Senior-care-focused PE firm; owner of Consulate Health Care and an earlier (2007) co-owner of Genesis Healthcare.

firms.name: GI Partners
firms.notes: Made a majority investment in ARS / American Residential Services in 2020; Charlesbank Capital Partners remains a co-owner.

firms.name: Goldman Sachs
firms.notes: Goldman Sachs Alternatives (the firm's private-equity business). Acquired Sila Services in early 2025.

tags.description: In Sept 2025 the Nexstar Network — the largest plumbing/HVAC trade group — severed ties with all PE-backed members (~1/3 of its 800 members) over the roll-up model; Forbes cited Sila's 28-acquisition consolidation as a leading example of the consolidation the group rejected.
Acquired Sila Services from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners in early 2025 in a roughly $1.5B sponsor-to-sponsor deal including debt — a leveraged continuation of the HVAC roll-up.

firms.name: Gryphon Investors
firms.notes: Owner of Smile Brands (originally acquired 2016, sold, re-acquired 2024).

tags.description: FTC consent orders (2022) required clinic divestitures and imposed prior-approval / prior-notice conditions on JAB's future specialty/emergency vet acquisitions (SAGE and Ethos matters).
Subject of a 2024 US Senate inquiry (Sens. Warren & Blumenthal) into consolidation and post-acquisition price increases at PE-owned vet clinics.
2023 recapitalization of PetVet used a ~$2.3B private loan to refinance over $3B of debt maturing from 2025.

firms.name: Leonard Green & Partners
firms.notes: Majority owner of Wrench Group (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) since 2019; TSG Consumer Partners and Oak Hill Capital took a minority stake in Nov 2022.

firms.name: Mars Veterinary Health
firms.notes: Family-owned CPG holding company; in scope as a holding company running a vet rollup.

tags.description: FTC required divestiture of 12 specialty/emergency clinics as a condition of the $9.1B VCA acquisition (2017), plus a 10-year FTC notice requirement.
Subject of a Nov 2024 US Senate investigation (Warren & Blumenthal) into Mars' impact on pet owners and veterinary workers.

firms.name: New Mountain Capital
firms.notes: Owns two DSOs: Benevis/Kool Smiles (acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020) and Western Dental / Sonrava Health (held since 2012).

firms.name: Oak Hill Capital
firms.notes: VetCor lead investor; co-owners Harvest Partners and Cressey & Company.

firms.name: OMERS Private Equity
firms.notes: Private-equity arm of the Canadian pension OMERS. Acquired TurnPoint Services from Trivest Partners in late 2020.

firms.name: Onex
firms.notes: Owner of SCP Health (formerly Schumacher Clinical Partners) since 2015.

firms.name: Pinta Capital Partners
firms.notes: PE group co-founded by Joel Landau; controls Genesis Healthcare through ReGen Healthcare (~93% equity). Genesis entered Chapter 11 in 2025.

tags.description: 2025 ~$8.6B recapitalization merging Southern Veterinary Partners + Mission Veterinary Partners included ~$3B of secured debt.

firms.name: Summit Partners
firms.notes: Led the 2018 buyout consortium for Sound Physicians (with Optum, Revelstoke and Silversmith).

firms.name: The Carlyle Group
firms.notes: Former owner of HCR ManorCare (2007–2018). Its LBO ended in the chain's 2018 bankruptcy.

firms.name: The Portopiccolo Group
firms.notes: PE firm (Simcha Hyman, Naftali Zanziper) that rolled up ~100 nursing facilities under brands including Accordius Health, Pelican Health and Orchid Cove.

tags.description: 2024–25 financial-press reporting documented persistent liquidity deficits at Thrive; the company engaged restructuring advisers and secured $350M+ of rescue financing.

businesses.name: Accordius Health
businesses.platform_company: Portopiccolo's nursing-home operating brand (part of a ~100-facility network incl. Pelican Health, Orchid Cove)

evidence.description: Investigative reporting (Axios, The New Yorker, Washington Post) documented steep staffing cuts and declining care after Portopiccolo acquisitions — including a Richmond-area (Henrico) nursing home where deaths doubled following the takeover, and a facility where some shifts had as few as two staff for 72 beds, with residents going days without care.

businesses.name: Apex Service Partners
businesses.platform_company: 100+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands; co-owners Partners Group and (2026) Apollo Global Management at a $10B valuation

businesses.name: ARS / Rescue Rooter (American Residential Services)
businesses.platform_company: ARS Network of HVAC/plumbing brands (Rescue Rooter, A.J. Perri, Blue Dot, Yes! and others); co-owner Charlesbank Capital Partners

evidence.description: Arizona AG consent judgment (April 2012, ~$395,000): resolved a 2011 lawsuit alleging ARS used false, misleading and deceptive sales tactics against (often older) consumers — including fake 'safety notices' to frighten buyers into unnecessary systems and official-looking solicitations — and undermined buyers' 3-day cancellation rights. ARS agreed to substantial changes in its sales practices. Predates GI Partners' 2020 ownership.

businesses.name: Aspen Dental
businesses.platform_company: 2nd-largest US DSO, 1,000+ locations in 46 states; co-owned by Leonard Green & Partners with a minority stake held by American Securities

evidence.description: California AG settlement (May 2026): Aspen agreed to $2M in penalties plus $300K restitution over alleged illegal corporate practice of dentistry and false/misleading advertising, with injunctive terms barring it from directing clinical practice or replacing practice-owner dentists of its choosing.

Massachusetts AG settlement announced Jan 5, 2023 ($3.5M): resolved a 2021 lawsuit alleging Aspen used bait-and-switch advertising — charging patients for exams/x-rays/screenings it advertised as free and claiming to accept all insurance when it did not accept MassHealth Medicaid. Aspen agreed to return up to $750K to affected patients.

businesses.name: Benevis / Kool Smiles
businesses.platform_company: Medicaid-focused DSO behind the Kool Smiles clinics; acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020 (prior owners: FFL Partners, then Tailwind Capital & Littlejohn)

evidence.description: US DOJ False Claims Act settlement (2018): Benevis and 130+ affiliated Kool Smiles clinics paid $23.9M to resolve allegations they billed Medicaid for medically unnecessary pediatric procedures — baby root canals, extractions and stainless-steel crowns on children (2009–2011) — with dentists pressured by production-quota bonuses. Settled without admission of wrongdoing. Conduct and settlement PREDATE New Mountain Capital's 2020 bankruptcy acquisition (then-owners FFL Partners, later Tailwind/Littlejohn).

businesses.name: Consulate Health Care
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US nursing-home providers, concentrated in Florida

evidence.description: False Claims Act case brought by whistleblower nurse Angela Ruckh: a federal jury found Consulate liable for 'upcoding' — billing Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary and inflated therapy. The judgment reached ~$258M; after appeals and six affiliated entities' bankruptcy filings, DOJ ultimately settled the judgment for $4.5M.

An analysis found a web of related companies made Consulate-owned nursing homes appear 'cash-strapped' — a related-party structure that moves money among affiliates while limiting the operators' apparent ability to pay judgments or invest in care.

businesses.name: Envision Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: EmCare (ER staffing) + AmSurg (ambulatory surgery); KKR's equity was wiped out in the May 2023 Chapter 11 — now owned by former creditors

evidence.description: Envision's EmCare unit was a central driver of the US surprise-billing crisis. A Yale study (Cooper & Scott Morton) of 2.2M ER visits found out-of-network billing rates jumped sharply after EmCare took over hospital emergency rooms — at ~15% of hospitals out-of-network rates exceeded 80% — exposing in-network patients to large surprise bills.

KKR took Envision private in 2018 in a $9.9B deal financed with ~$7B of debt (~70% of the price). When the No Surprises Act (2022) ended its lucrative out-of-network billing model, the debt load became unsustainable and Envision filed Chapter 11 in May 2023 — one of the largest PE-backed healthcare bankruptcies. KKR's equity was wiped out and creditors took control.

businesses.name: Genesis Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: ~175 skilled-nursing/assisted-living facilities in 18 states; originally taken private by Formation Capital & JER Partners in 2007; filed Chapter 11 in July 2025 (an insider sale to ReGen/Pinta was rejected by the court in Dec 2025)

evidence.description: $53.6M DOJ settlement (2017): Genesis resolved allegations it billed Medicare/Medicaid for medically unnecessary therapy and hospice services and provided 'grossly substandard' care with inadequate staffing — much of the conduct at acquired operators Skilled Healthcare and Sun Healthcare (2005–2013).

Genesis filed for Chapter 11 in July 2025 with more than $2.3B in debt, threatening care for residents across 18 states. Sens. Warren & Blumenthal and Reps. Goodlander & Welch opened an investigation into the PE-driven bankruptcy's impact on nursing-home and assisted-living residents.

businesses.name: HCR ManorCare
businesses.platform_company: Then the 2nd-largest US nursing-home chain; after Carlyle's LBO collapsed it was acquired out of 2018 bankruptcy by ProMedica (a nonprofit)

evidence.description: Carlyle took HCR ManorCare private in 2007 for $6.3B, three-quarters funded by debt. A 2011 sale-leaseback sold the company's real estate for $6.1B — recouping Carlyle's ~$1.3B equity — but left the chain paying rent it increasingly couldn't afford. It filed for bankruptcy in March 2018.

As ManorCare cut costs and laid off staff, health-code violations rose 26% between 2013 and 2017. State inspectors found residents left unattended — call buttons so poorly staffed that some residents regularly soiled themselves waiting for help to the bathroom (Washington Post investigation).

businesses.name: Heartland Dental
businesses.platform_company: Largest US DSO — 1,900+ affiliated practices across 39 states + DC; Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan retains a minority stake

businesses.name: Mission Pet Health
businesses.platform_company: Southern Veterinary Partners + Mission Veterinary Partners; co-owned with Shore Capital

businesses.name: SCP Health
businesses.platform_company: 4th-largest US emergency-medicine staffing firm (~258 emergency departments; 7,500+ clinicians across 36 states)

businesses.name: Sila Services
businesses.platform_company: 30+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands across the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest; acquired from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners

businesses.name: Smile Brands
businesses.platform_company: 75+ affiliated brands including Affordable Care; Gryphon re-acquired the DSO in 2024

businesses.name: Sound Physicians
businesses.platform_company: Hospitalist + emergency-medicine staffing; 2018 ~$2.15B buyout led by Summit Partners with Optum (UnitedHealth), Revelstoke and Silversmith

businesses.name: TeamHealth
businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US emergency-medicine and hospital physician staffing firms

evidence.description: ProPublica documented how TeamHealth, under Blackstone, used out-of-network emergency-room billing to mark up patient bills — a model that generated large surprise bills for insured patients who had no choice of ER physician.

US DOJ False Claims Act settlement ($60M, 2017): TeamHealth, as successor to IPC Healthcare, resolved allegations of 'upcoding' — billing Medicare, Medicaid, the Defense Health Agency and the federal employee program for higher and more expensive levels of service than were actually provided. Originated as a qui tam whistleblower suit; TeamHealth entered a 5-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

businesses.name: Thrive Pet Healthcare
businesses.platform_company: formerly Pathway Vet Alliance

businesses.name: TurnPoint Services
businesses.platform_company: HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform; brands include Southern Home Services; acquired from Trivest Partners

businesses.name: VetCor
businesses.platform_company: co-owned with Harvest Partners and Cressey & Company

businesses.name: Western Dental / Sonrava Health
businesses.platform_company: Rebranded Sonrava Health; one of the longest-held PE dental platforms (since 2012); a 2024 sale process did not complete

businesses.name: Wrench Group
businesses.platform_company: 25+ HVAC/plumbing/electrical brands; minority co-investors TSG Consumer Partners, Oak Hill Capital, AustralianSuper, Crescent Capital
